summary: Spun out of MPI-387 after the 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0 in-app update ran live for the first time and failed. The OLD path died on stdio:ignore (shell-redirect capture always 0 bytes); the NEW win-update.cjs is immune by construction but has two gaps found auditing it. (1) Silent by construction - Electron spawns it detached with stdio ignore so there is no console any more, and it writes no log file, so a failure quits the app with no window, no message and no evidence - the MPI-369 blindness class on a new path. (2) The MpiOkCancel copy promises the app will reopen; win-update.cjs ends at Update applied successfully with no relaunch, and neither update-from-zip.bat has one. Also carries two 1.4.0-gated validation items inherited from MPI-387: a SECOND update from the new layout (the only thing exercising loadExtractZip resources/app branch + evictBusyFile) and in-app fetch+spawn on the new path. Code fixes should land BEFORE 1.4.0 so a failed validation leaves something to read.

Validated live and moved to doing. The user ran the shipped 1.3.0 portable at D:\cubric-install-test, took the prompt, pressed Update, and reported nothing happened - but the update FULLY SUCCEEDED: fetch-release pulled CubricVision-windows-x64-update-v1.3.1.zip (1166674 bytes), apply-update backed up to update/rollback/2026-08-03T03-44-16-461Z and wrote resources/app at APP_VERSION 1.3.1, confirmed by a relaunch showing V1.3.1 in the app header. So validation item 2 (in-app fetch+spawn on the new win-update.cjs path) PASSES, and loadExtractZip took its resources/app branch. evictBusyFile is still unexercised - the delta shipped no CubricVision.exe. What the user experienced is exactly the two carded gaps: no console, no log file, and no relaunch. Fixing both now.

Both code gaps FIXED and verified live against the 1.3.1 install. (1) win-update.cjs now tees itself plus BOTH helpers stdout and stderr to update/update.log truncated per run - runHelper piped stderr instead of inheriting it from a NUL parent, so the real fetch-release reason appeared for the first time. (2) Relaunch on BOTH outcomes, targeting root CubricVision.exe not process.execPath (evictBusyFile can have renamed the running image aside) with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE deleted from the child env. (3) Failure writes update/update-result.json carrying the last helper stderr line, new main.js update-last-result IPC reads-and-deletes it, updateChecker raises showError and skips that boots update prompt so two dialogs never stack. (4) Same marker + relaunch on update.sh and update.command, logging to a file only when stdout is not a tty so a double-clicked run keeps its terminal output AND its real exit status. Evidence: bogus-repo run wrote log + valid marker + relaunched; real-repo run re-applied the 1.3.1 delta from the resources/app layout and cold-relaunched the app (0 processes to 6, fresh boot in app.log); a planted marker made the app log previous update run failed and raise the dialog. Test install restored to clean 1.3.1, all three files hash-matched. 314/314 node tests pass, eslint clean. NOT closed: the fix cannot help 1.3.1 to 1.4.0 because the updater that runs is the one already on disk - it first takes effect 1.4.0 to 1.5.0, and 1.4.0 release notes must tell users to reopen manually. evictBusyFile still unexercised.

CLOSED - every gap fixed and every inherited validation item settled, none of it deferred to 1.4.0. Two fakes replaced the two things that looked like they needed a real newer GitHub release, and neither needed an upload. (a) evictBusyFile, unexercised since MPI-387: apply-update accepts an already-extracted DIRECTORY as its bundle (the MPI-62 Safari path), so a folder holding a copy of CubricVision.exe plus a manifest listing that one file is a complete update bundle - run through CubricVision.exe as node the target is genuinely busy. The Aug 1 image moved to CubricVision.exe.old and the new one landed at the original path. (b) The in-app button end-to-end: check-for-update reads require(./package.json).version, so stamping the install back to 1.3.0 makes the LIVE 1.3.1 release genuinely newer - real compare, real prompt, real user click, real fetch, real apply, real relaunch, button to running-again in about 3 seconds, confirmed on screen. CORRECTION to this brief: its claim that process.execPath can be the retired binary is WRONG. Measured - with the running image renamed aside mid-flight a live electron-as-node process still reported the original CubricVision.exe path, because Node captures execPath once at bootstrap and eviction leaves that path holding the NEW binary. Root path kept for being explicit, not because execPath is broken; doc corrected. Install restored to pristine 1.3.1, three files hash-matched. Residual, NOT blocking: the Linux and macOS updaters were changed but never run (sh -n only, no box), and 1.4.0 users still get 1.3.1 silent updater - the release-note requirement is now in github-release-checklist.md where it will actually be read.
